Home/How it works
THE WORKFLOW

From your experience
to a plan for the week.

Move from your own experience to a direction you can test, then into a local workspace for the job search itself.

Example: A software engineer considering platform work reviews an achievement about a release, picks a direction to test, and sets aside 30 minutes to compare that achievement with one job requirement. The result is a next action and a clearer gap to investigate.

01Gather evidence
02Explore directions
03Build a plan
04Work your search
01

Start with what you know.

Set out your experience, the kind of work you’re considering and the time you can give each week. Add achievements manually or connect them to exact quotations from private project-note or résumé excerpts. The recovery app accepts up to 15 achievement claims and up to three source excerpts.

02

Check your evidence.

Confirm, reject or leave a claim unverified. Corrections preserve a history and reset confirmation, so a changed statement doesn’t silently retain old evidence links. Compare supplied job requirements against achievements you have confirmed yourself.

Read the evidence methodology ↗
03

Choose something to test.

Return to similar work, shift toward a new kind of work, or explore a stepping-stone role. Every direction states its unknowns. Choose one to generate a seven-day plan bounded by your available hours, then mark actions complete and record what you learned.

04

Bring focus to your search.

The integrated workspace opens the job-search workspace for discovery, CV work, research and application tracking. Recovery context stays visible, but CVs, evidence and job targets aren’t automatically synchronized between the two systems.

Your starting point can be small. Core recovery works without an AI key, a hosted account or a résumé upload. Optional AI and job-search integrations are configured separately.
